sections.content_markdown:
A clause is a group of words that contains a subject and a predicate.

There are two kinds of clauses: independent and subordinate clauses. A clause may be either a sentence (an independent clause) or a sentence-like construction within another sentence (a dependent or subordinate clause).

### The Independent Clause

An independent clause expresses a complete thought and can stand by itself as a sentence. If you recognize a sentence, you should be able to recognize independent clauses.

Look at the following examples:

* Many people are afraid of tornadoes.
* A tornado can be terrifying.
* A tornado is a violently revolving storm.
* In the centre of the tornado is an area of calm air.
* The centre of the tornado is known as the "eye".
* This eye is formed by the air spiraling around it.
* This eye is simply a hollow space.

All the above sentences are independent clauses. A sentence may have more than one independent clause.
